rounds.text: Uma Exports Ltd is currently trading at a significant discount to its underlying assets, with a price-to-book ratio of just 0.38x [E2], which is notably lower than the sector benchmark of 1.56x [E7]. The company has demonstrated a strong commitment to balance sheet health by aggressively reducing borrowings from Rs 212 Cr to Rs 142 Cr in the last year [E35], [E55]. This deleveraging is supported by a robust cash position, evidenced by a cash conversion ratio of 63.00x and operating cash flow of Rs 63 Cr, which fully backs reported profits [E29], [E30]. Furthermore, the completion of capital expenditure, indicated by CWIP falling to Rs 0 Cr, suggests that new capacity is now coming online to drive future performance [E36]. While the company has shown recent profit growth of 104% [E19], it is important to note that this follows a period of inconsistent margins [E27], [E28]. Conceded: the company faces challenges with a high P/E ratio [E1], a lack of dividend payouts [E4], [E57], and a recent decline in promoter holding [E37], [E59]. Despite these headwinds, the business operates within a sector currently experiencing a positive tailwind [E69], [E70].
